Since you're targeting Product-Based companies

Trust me—your database knowledge must be strong in query optimization, indexing, transactions, locking mechanisms, partitioning, and database system design.

➊ 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐬 & 𝐀𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞
Understand how databases work, their components, and architecture.

 ↳ Database types (Relational, NoSQL)
 ↳ ACID properties & CAP theorem
 ↳ DBMS vs. RDBMS vs. NoSQL
 ↳ Database Storage Engines (InnoDB vs. MyISAM)
 ↳ Database Architecture (Single-tier, Two-tier, Three-tier)

➋ 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐱𝐢𝐧𝐠 & 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐎𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Improve query performance with indexing & optimization techniques.

 ↳ Types of Indexes (Clustered, Non-clustered, Composite, Unique, Full-text, Bitmap)
 ↳ How Indexing Works (B-Trees, Hash Indexing, etc.)
 ↳ Indexing Best Practices & When NOT to Use Indexes
 ↳ Query Execution Plan (EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
 ↳ Optimizing Joins, Sorting, and Aggregations

➌ 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 & 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐥
Ensure consistency and integrity in multi-user database environments.

 ↳ ACID properties in transactions
 ↳ Transaction isolation levels (READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE)
 ↳ Locking mechanisms (Pessimistic vs. Optimistic)
 ↳ Deadlocks – Causes & Prevention
 ↳ Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC)

➍ 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 & 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠
Scale databases by distributing data efficiently.

 ↳ Horizontal vs. Vertical Partitioning
 ↳ Range, List, Hash, and Composite Partitioning
 ↳ Sharding Strategies (Key-based, Range-based, Directory-based)
 ↳ Challenges in Sharding (Data consistency, Cross-shard queries)
 ↳ Replication vs. Sharding

➎ 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 & 𝐍𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Design efficient, scalable database schemas.

 ↳ Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling
 ↳ Normal Forms (1NF to 5NF)
 ↳ Denormalization & When to Use It
 ↳ Star vs. Snowflake Schema (Data Warehousing)
 ↳ Handling One-to-Many & Many-to-Many Relationships

➏ 𝐒𝐐𝐋 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐓𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠
Optimize SQL queries for high performance.

 ↳ Writing Efficient SQL Queries
 ↳ Avoiding Full Table Scans
 ↳ Use of Proper Indexing Strategies
 ↳ Query Execution Plans & Optimization Techniques
 ↳ Materialized Views & Caching

➐ 𝐍𝐨𝐒𝐐𝐋 𝐯𝐬. 𝐒𝐐𝐋 – 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐨 𝐔𝐬𝐞 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭?
Choosing the right database for the right use case.

 ↳ SQL vs. NoSQL (Key differences)
 ↳ Types of NoSQL Databases (Document, Key-Value, Columnar, Graph)
 ↳ When to Use NoSQL Over SQL
 ↳ CAP Theorem & BASE Properties in NoSQL
 ↳ Examples: MongoDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB

Get the interview call: https://lnkd.in/ges-e-7J
Join me: https://lnkd.in/giE3e9yH

ai_analysis.summary: This is a database-focused interview-preparation checklist for candidates targeting product-based companies. It emphasizes query optimization, indexing, transactions, locking, partitioning, and database system design, then groups study topics into database architecture, concurrency control, partitioning and sharding, data modeling, SQL performance tuning, and SQL versus NoSQL selection. The post lists many concepts without explaining them in depth and ends with promotional links and a visible "see more" marker.
subtopics: Single-tier, two-tier, and three-tier database architecture
Clustered, non-clustered, composite, unique, full-text, and bitmap indexes
Indexing best practices and cases when indexes should not be used
Query execution plans and EXPLAIN ANALYZE
Range, list, hash, and composite partitioning
Data consistency and cross-shard query challenges
Document, key-value, columnar, and graph NoSQL databases

interview_questions.question: Which database fundamentals should a candidate be prepared to discuss?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer distinguishes database types and the DBMS, RDBMS, and NoSQL categories.
The answer identifies single-tier, two-tier, and three-tier architectures and mentions InnoDB and MyISAM storage engines.
The answer includes ACID properties and CAP theorem within the relevant database topics.

interview_questions.question: How would you investigate and improve the performance of a slow SQL query?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer uses a query execution plan and EXPLAIN ANALYZE as part of the investigation.
The answer considers whether the query is causing a full table scan or has expensive joins, sorting, or aggregations.
The answer evaluates suitable clustered, non-clustered, composite, unique, full-text, or bitmap indexes and recognizes cases when an index should not be used.
The answer considers materialized views or caching where appropriate.

interview_questions.question: How do the listed transaction isolation levels and concurrency-control mechanisms differ?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer discusses READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels.
The answer contrasts pessimistic locking with optimistic locking.
The answer includes deadlock causes and prevention and identifies MVCC as a concurrency-control mechanism.

interview_questions.question: How do partitioning, sharding, and replication relate when scaling a database?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer distinguishes horizontal partitioning from vertical partitioning.
The answer identifies range, list, hash, and composite partitioning methods.
The answer compares key-based, range-based, and directory-based sharding strategies.
The answer recognizes data consistency and cross-shard queries as sharding challenges and distinguishes replication from sharding.

interview_questions.question: How would you design a relational data model and decide whether to normalize or denormalize it?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer uses ER modeling and addresses one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.
The answer distinguishes the listed normal forms from 1NF through 5NF.
The answer explains that denormalization is a deliberate option to consider rather than treating normalization as the only listed modeling approach.
The answer identifies Star and Snowflake schemas as data warehousing design choices.

interview_questions.question: When would SQL be preferable to NoSQL, and when would NoSQL be considered?
interview_questions.answer:
The answer compares SQL and NoSQL using the post's stated database-selection criteria.
The answer recognizes document, key-value, columnar, and graph categories of NoSQL databases.
The answer relates CAP theorem and BASE properties to the selection discussion.
The answer uses only the named examples MongoDB, Cassandra, and DynamoDB when examples are required.
